points.t: Occlusion, urine, faecal enzymes and friction break the barrier; Candida loves damaged moist skin.
Frequent changes, nappy-free time, thick barrier ointment; add hydrocortisone 1% or an azole.
Unwell infant, under 1 month, ulceration, non-response, safeguarding.

points: **Faecal enzymes** and bile salts damage the barrier; ammonia raises the pH.
Friction, plus an atopic or seborrhoeic tendency.
*Candida albicans* thrives on damaged skin. Not usually nappy allergy, and **not tinea**.
**Irritant**: redness ± scale or erosions on **convex** skin; folds spared.
**Candidal**: bright red, shiny, **into the folds**, with **satellite** papules and pustules.
**Impetigo**: irregular blisters, pustules or honey crust.

visuals.caption: Irritant napkin dermatitis (left): redness on the convex skin touching the nappy, creases spared. Candidal (right): beefy red rash running into the creases with satellite spots beyond the edge.
visuals.alt: Infant nappy area comparing irritant and candidal napkin dermatitis

points: Check the **folds** and look for satellites.
If severe, atypical or not responding.
Refractory: **zinc deficiency** (acrodermatitis enteropathica) or **Langerhans cell histiocytosis**: specialist.
Injury pattern that does not fit dermatitis: document and escalate locally.

cards.name: Candida
cards.clue: Folds involved; satellite papules and pustules.

manage.lead: Aligned with NICE CKS nappy rash and PCDS; check BNF for Children.

points: Water or non-soap cleanser; pat dry; no fragranced wipes.
**Thick barrier ointment** (petrolatum ± zinc oxide) at **every change**.

rx.dur: Short course, usually up to 7 days
rx.note: No potent steroids on nappy skin.

rx.dur: Continue after clear; often 7–14 days in total

points: Follow local guidance: oral flucloxacillin if needed.
Topical fusidic acid only for very localised areas.

limits.t: Not for the nappy area in primary care.
Parents often use too little: show them.

items.t: Infant **under 1 month** with significant rash, or a **systemically unwell** infant.
Bruising or a pattern suggesting **non-accidental injury**: safeguarding.
Severe or **ulcerated** rash, or no improvement with good care and treatment.
Diagnostic doubt, or suspected nutritional deficiency or rare disease.

pearls.t: Demonstrate a thick layer of barrier ointment at every change.
Mild hydrocortisone for a short course is fine; potent steroids are not.
Breastfed stools are less alkaline: supportive counselling, not a treatment claim.

quiz.q: Folds spared or involved: which suggests Candida?
quiz.a: Involved folds with satellite papules/pustules suggest Candida; spared folds suggest irritant.

quiz.q: What goes on at every nappy change?
quiz.a: A thick barrier ointment (petrolatum ± zinc oxide).

quiz.q: Steroid choice and duration for inflamed irritant nappy rash?
quiz.a: Hydrocortisone 1%, thin layer, short course (usually up to 7 days). No potent steroids.

quiz.q: Rash refractory to good care: which rarities?
quiz.a: Zinc deficiency (acrodermatitis enteropathica) and Langerhans cell histiocytosis: specialist input.
Under 1 month with significant rash, or systemically unwell.
